title: Will AI make your degree pointless?
description:
AI isn’t just occasionally going rogue…(Open AI and Meta we’re looking at you) it’s also changing the world of work. Nearly 70% of college students in the US said they thought AI would make it harder to find a job in a recent survey - and 22% said that they’ve changed what they’re deciding to study at university because of this. They’re not the only ones… students all over the world are thinking about how to AI-proof their future careers.

In this episode, we go to the University College London campus to speak to three students: Omer, who’s studying French and German, Zahra, who’s studying entrepreneurship, and Allie, who’s just graduated from Kings College after completing her law studies. They tell us how they think AI could change the course of their careers, how they’re adapting to the new technology, and if their degrees will still be helpful in the face of AI.

summaryZh: 本集 BBC 節目《What in the World》探討人工智慧 AI 對大學學位與職涯前景的衝擊，並採訪三位來自倫敦的大學生與畢業生。修讀語言學的 Omar 表示，書面翻譯雖易被 AI 取代，但面對面溝通、情感連結與文化脈絡仍無法被科技取代。法律系畢業生 Ali 指出，法律界正積極導入 AI 技術，但由於 AI 容易產生錯誤與「幻覺」，始終需要人類嚴格監督。主修創業學的 Zara 則保持樂觀，主張結合人類領導與 AI 技術以創造優勢。三位受訪者均認為，大學所培養的人際技能與生活體驗無法被取代，學子應選擇能與 AI 互補的專業，積極運用科技打造未來的職涯防護。
summaryEn: In this episode of BBC's What in the World, host Hannah Gelbart visits University College London (UCL) to discuss with three students and graduates—Omer (studying languages), Zara (studying entrepreneurship), and Allie (a law graduate)—how AI is impacting their future careers and the value of their degrees. Omer highlights that while written translation can be automated, real human connection and cultural nuances remain irreplaceable. Allie notes that although law firms are embracing AI tools, human oversight is still crucial because AI models are prone to errors and hallucinations. Zara sees AI as an exciting opportunity, advocating for a hybrid model that balances human leadership with technology. Overall, the guests agree that university provides vital life experiences and interpersonal skills, advising future students to pursue their passions while using AI as a complementary tool.

I think all of us gain have gained so much from our from our degrees, different skills and I think university is also just broader and bigger than just academic side of it.

There really is, it's a luxury to have a university degree and to have 3 years to to think about a subject that you are, hopefully, passionate about and to think about the different sides of it and have the teachers and textbooks available to you for for questions.

My advice would be to still follow your dreams, follow your passions, but make sure that what you are get, do your research, of course, but make sure that the subjects that your degree has to offer are complementary.
